_comment: DS4 machine tuning profiles. The first entry whose match{chip substring, min_ram_gib} fits this machine is applied: each env var is set as a DEFAULT (setenv overwrite=0), so anything you export yourself still wins. Generate/refresh an entry for your machine with ./tune_profile.sh. Order entries most-specific first.

_backends_reference._doc: Valid 'backend' values for prefill_by_tokens — the resident routed-MoE prefill algorithm, selected PER PREFILL CHUNK by token count. PRECEDENCE: (1) env param DS4_RESIDENT_MOE_BACKEND forces one backend for all chunks; (2) this prefill_by_tokens table (the loader encodes it into DS4_RESIDENT_MOE_PREFILL_BY_TOKENS and the engine resolves the backend by name per chunk); (3) the predefined env gates (NAX_HALF + MIN_TOKENS, to be phased out). Backends honored PER-CHUNK in the grouped path: mulmm, nax_half, nax_half_alu, nax_int8 (the table overrides the static env flags). ane_gpu is per-chunk switchable by routing that chunk into the resident ANE dedup orchestrator; ane_alu/ane_nax/pathc are unsupported in the grouped path — naming any of them in a range logs a one-time warning and falls back to the env gates. NAX backends are M5+ only (matmul2d); on M3/M4 they fall back to mul_mm_id. NAX-half additionally requires n_tokens % 64 == 0 (else the engine uses int8).

mulmm.desc: Upstream mul_mm_id grouped GPU matmul (pure ALU, no NAX). The 'ALU only' baseline. Works on all chips.

nax_int8.desc: NAX int8 matmul2d, compact-bridge fused-dequant. M5 LARGE-chunk winner.
nax_int8.env: DS4_RESIDENT_MOE_MPP_INT8_PREFILL=1 DS4_RESIDENT_MOE_MPP_COMPACT_BRIDGE=1 DS4_RESIDENT_MOE_MPP_FUSED_DEQUANT=1 (+MPP_FORCE=1 to ignore the auto min-tokens gate)

nax_half.desc: NAX half x half matmul2d (no fused gate+up).

nax_half_alu.desc: NAX-half + ALU, Plan A fused gate+up+swiglu. CORRECT (FIXED 2026-06-01, commit aeea2b7: was reducing only 32 of K + dropping the routing weight; now matches mulmm/nax_half exactly) and ~6% faster than plain nax_half. BUT no longer used in the M5 profile: re-benchmarked on the fixed kernel (mult-of-64 chunks, verified mode=half), nax_int8 is FASTER at every <8K chunk (2048: int8 255 vs half_alu 224; 4096: 358 vs 325; 6144: 414 vs 382) — int8 improved (was 269@4096) so the old cool crossover no longer holds. Kept available; re-bake on a cool box if you want to re-check the crossover.

pathc.desc: Path C: i8 in-kernel NAX-parallel-ALU full-fused.
pathc.note: ~tie with nax_int8 on M5 (no cross-kernel NAX/ALU overlap)

ane_gpu.desc: ANE hot experts + overlapped per-expert GPU gather/scatter cold tail. Resident/full-model ANE dedup path used by the M3U resident profile; sidecar Flash-MoE has its own sidecar_env and uses SSD GPU-dedup + ANE/GPU overlap scheduler.

ane_alu.desc: ANE hot + grouped classic-int8 (mul_mm_id) cold. Correct — identical to ane_gpu's cold tail (the per-expert dedup compute it once used is broken and is no longer on this path).

ane_nax.desc: ANE hot + grouped NAX cold (resident NAX-half/int8 under the ANE skip mask). Correct (validate_ane_nax 8/8). NOT a throughput win yet on M5 Max: the cold tail runs SEQUENTIALLY after ANE drains, and resident-NAX cold is slower to encode than fused mul_mm_id, so ane_nax<ane_gpu (measured ctx16384: 207 vs 315 t/s). The win needs true ANE-parallel-NAX overlap (dispatch NAX before draining ANE) — not yet implemented. Off by default.
ane_nax.chips: M5+; correct but not faster (no overlap yet)

profiles._comment: M5 Max 128G, MEASURED (81G IQ2XXS, 45s cooldown, alone on box). CORRECTED 2026-06-01: (a) added DS4_METAL_PREFILL_CHUNK=16384 — without it a bare ./ds4 auto-caps the chunk to 4096 (<sync_max_tokens 7168) and the resident-NAX path takes the slow CPU<->GPU count-readback (map_wait) sync bridge; CTX_GROW_BLOCK is the KV-growth block, NOT the prefill chunk. (b) reverted the >1000->ane_gpu routing back to the NAX crossover: ane_gpu (ANE+GPU dedup) MEASURED 30-41% SLOWER on M5 single-cluster (ctx16384: ane_gpu 310 vs nax_half_alu 445 vs nax_int8 526 t/s) because ANE_HYBRID forces the 2048-token scratch tile -> sync bridge ON. prefill_by_tokens picks per prefill chunk: nax_half_alu below 7680 tok, nax_int8 at/above (crossover from 4096:316/269 .. 7168:423/366 half-wins .. 8192:378/500 int8-wins; loader maps to NAX_HALF_MAX_TOKENS=7680). With chunk 16384 production prefill resolves to nax_int8 (~526 hot). Verify with the 'resident-NAX tile n_tokens=.. sync-bridge=off' startup line. 2026-06-01 (FINAL): the whole range is now nax_int8. History: <7680 was nax_half_alu (Plan A fused); the fused kernel diverged (reduced only 32 of K + dropped routing weight) -> FIXED in commit aeea2b7 (rewritten to mirror the validated h_h_f matmul, dynamic_extent K, + weighted scatter; now matches mulmm/nax_half exactly). Then re-benchmarked the FIXED kernel on the same box (mult-of-64 chunks, verified mode=half/fused_experts>0): nax_int8 is FASTER at every <8K chunk (2048: 255 vs 224, 4096: 358 vs 325, 6144: 414 vs 382) AND >=8K (526 vs 445) -> route everything to nax_int8. The old cool crossover (half_alu<7680) no longer holds because nax_int8 got faster (269->358 @4096). nax_half_alu stays correct + available; re-bake cool if you want to re-test.
profiles._sidecar_comment: M5 Max 128G streaming (Flash-MoE slot-bank) — applied when --moe-mode slot-bank + --moe-sidecar (g_profile_sidecar_mode). MEASURED 2026-06-02 (slots=96, prompts coding_*, single gen tok): routed-on-ANE beats routed-on-GPU/NAX-int8 across the board (4K +14.8%, 2K chunk +18.7%; shrinks to +3% by 16K chunk as the SSD I/O bubble closes). Single-cluster M5: ANE_DUAL=0 THREADS=1, shared-expert+O-proj ANE off. min_refs 32-64 (NOT 384 — too conservative). Resident path (env+prefill_by_tokens above) stays SINGLE-SEGMENT nax_int8: a crossover (ane_gpu for <8K chunks) is tempting from per-chunk data but the ane* segment forces ANE_HYBRID=1 globally -> 2048 scratch tile -> sync bridge on the 16384 nax_int8 chunk too. MEASURED 2026-06-02 (same 17K-token prompt): crossover '8191:ane_gpu,99999:nax_int8' = 185 t/s vs pure nax_int8 = 494 t/s (-63%). Do NOT multi-segment resident on M5. HYBRID_ANE_MIN_REFS=64 confirmed by the slots=99 sweep (best at 4K/8K/16K).

profiles._comment: M3 Ultra 128G+ — resident/full-model defaults to resident ane_gpu with per-expert GPU gather/scatter cold tail overlapped with ANE. Do not force DS4_RESIDENT_MOE_BACKEND here: that env var has higher precedence and would bypass the table. Flash-MoE sidecar uses a separate sidecar_env so SSD slot-bank runs get GPU dedup + ANE/GPU overlap scheduler without inheriting resident-only knobs.

M3 Ultra 96G — resident/full-model keeps the 1becf06 resident-memory growth block (2048) plus 16K prefill chunk. Re-baked 2026-06-02 on M3U/96G: resident GPU/ALU wins 1K-8K (255/299/335/324 t/s vs ANE 155/219/278/285), resident ANE wins the 16K full-chunk case (237 vs 196) and is roughly tied/slightly ahead at 32K (228 vs 226 on the generated 36.4K-token prompt). The resident table therefore routes tiny chunks to ANE, mid chunks to mulmm, and 16K-class chunks to ane_gpu; long prompts get ANE on full 16K chunks while their small tail stays on GPU/ALU. Do not force DS4_RESIDENT_MOE_BACKEND here: that env var has higher precedence and would bypass the table. Flash-MoE sidecar uses a separate sidecar_env so SSD slot-bank runs get GPU dedup + ANE/GPU overlap scheduler without inheriting resident-only knobs; the same M3U/96G sweep showed sidecar ANE wins from ~2K upward (8K 296 vs 253), while 512/1K remain GPU-favored and can be forced with DS4_FLASH_MOE_ANE_PREFILL=0 for short-prompt tests.

M5 Max 96G — mirrors the 128G entry (same single-ANE-cluster silicon; the ANE-slow finding is RAM-independent). CORRECTED 2026-06-01: was an ANE-dedup config (ane_gpu-style), which is 30-41% slower on M5 single-cluster; switched to the NAX resident config with DS4_METAL_PREFILL_CHUNK=16384 + nax_int8 routing for large chunks. 81G model fits in 96G. Retest/re-bake with tune_profile.sh on a 96G M5 Max if available.
profiles._sidecar_comment: M5 Max 96G streaming — mirrors the 128G sidecar_env (same single-ANE-cluster silicon). Routed-on-ANE streaming config; resident env/prefill_by_tokens stays nax_int8. See the 128G _sidecar_comment and moe-batch-bench/PREFILL_PROFILE_M5MAX.md.

profiles._comment: M5 Max <96G — STREAMING ONLY. The 81G IQ2_XXS model cannot be resident under 96G RAM, so this entry has NO resident env/prefill_by_tokens; only sidecar_env (Flash-MoE slot-bank). Same single-ANE-cluster streaming config as the 128G/96G sidecar_env, validated end-to-end (slots=99: 'applied sidecar tuning profile [Apple M5 Max]' + 'routed experts = ANE i8i8 (W8A8)', no env flags). Slot count is a CLI arg (--moe-slot-bank), pick for your RAM (slots=99 ~ 40G RSS). Catches 48-95G M5 Max; ordered after the >=96G entries so they win for resident-capable machines. See moe-batch-bench/PROFILE_NEW_MACHINE.md.

M1 Max 64G — STREAMING (Flash-MoE SSD/slot-bank). GPU/ALU (mul_mm_id) routed-MoE prefill, ANE OFF. MEASURED 2026-06-02 (slots=96, coding_* prompts, single gen tok, cooldown'd): single-cluster ANE LOSES to GPU/ALU at every config tested. Cool 8K GPU=94.31 t/s vs best-tuned ANE (tiled-fused, max_refs=512, batches=256/512, min_refs=512)=90.63 (-3.9%); ANE never wins at any min_refs/max_refs/batch schedule. Findings: (a) routed-ANE only works on the tiled-fused kernel — fp16x/full-fused set I8I8_TILED_FUSED=0 which silently disables routing (ane_refs=0 = secret GPU, do NOT use). (b) throughput-bound, not padding-bound: bigger ANE batches (max_refs 512) beat smaller despite ~32% pad waste; multi-bucket batch schedules (128,256 / 64,128,256) cut padding but didn't raise t/s. (c) ANE/GPU overlap already near-perfect (overlap scheduler est_idle ~0.5%) so no overlap headroom. (d) the earlier '+8% ANE win' was a THERMAL artifact (measured vs a hot 83.91 GPU; real cool GPU is 94.31). M1 Max has no NAX (M5-only) so the GPU path is mul_mm_id ALU. To A/B ANE on, export DS4_FLASH_MOE_ANE_PREFILL=1 (+ tiled-fused, max_refs=512). KV growth block 2048 (conservative for 64 GiB single-die). MEMORY BUDGET (64 GiB): slots=64 default — slots=96 + large ctx (e.g. --ctx 100000) over-commits RAM and SWAPS (8.8G dense + ~28G 96-slot bank + KV > 64G; prefill collapses to ~2 t/s, MEASURED). 64 fits; raise slots only at small ctx. The recorded prefill benchmarks used slots=96 at small ctx (<=20K, no swap). See moe-batch-bench/run_*_M1MAX64.sh + sweep harness.
